header.userPrompt:
Add a generic DB-backed rate limiter and use it to stop Bedrock throttling from permanently failing statement drafts. Implements issue #119.

## Problem
Uploading several bank statements in a short window makes some drafts end up status=failed with a raw AWS error in the UI (a BedrockRuntime ThrottlingException / HTTP 429). Extraction runs as a background job and each draft fans out into several Bedrock `converse` calls via StatementExtractionService; confirmed statements also enqueue ResolveStatementSuggestions jobs that call Bedrock again. A burst exceeds the account's per-minute Bedrock quota. Today ExtractBankStatementDraftAction catches every exception and marks the DRAFT failed, so the job itself succeeds and never retries, and the raw SDK string reaches the user.

The app is stateless, so the rate limiter must be stateless too: DB-backed, no in-process counters.

## Design (agreed — follow exactly)

Use the limiter as ADMISSION CONTROL: the Bedrock client REJECTS fast when no slot is free, and the existing background-job retry/backoff provides the waiting. Do NOT make the client block/wait for a slot.

### 1. Generic rate-limit table (one row per key, self-resetting)
Add a Play evolution (the next number after the highest existing file in server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/). Table `rate_limit_window`:
- key TEXT NOT NULL
- window_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
- count INT NOT NULL
- PRIMARY KEY (key)

No CHECK constraints, no column DEFAULTs (app-level only, per repo conventions). The table stores ONLY these three columns. Because there is exactly one row per key and it self-resets on minute rollover, the table never grows: there must be NO expiry job and NO cleanup sweep.

### 2. Atomic consume (single statement, no check-then-write race)
Acquire one slot with a single statement; a returned row means the slot was granted, no row means over the limit this minute:

    INSERT INTO rate_limit_window (key, window_start, count)
    VALUES ({key}, date_trunc('minute', now()), 1)
    ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE
    SET window_start = date_trunc('minute', now()),
        count = CASE
          WHEN rate_limit_window.window_start = date_trunc('minute', now())
            THEN rate_limit_window.count + 1
          ELSE 1
        END
    WHERE rate_limit_window.window_start < date_trunc('minute', now())
       OR rate_limit_window.count < {limit}
    RETURNING count;

This must be one atomic statement (the ON CONFLICT row lock makes it race-free) — do NOT implement it as a SELECT then UPDATE/INSERT (that is a check-then-write race and is explicitly disallowed by the repo's coding-patterns reviewer).

### 3. RateLimiter service + Anorm DAO/repository
Expose `tryAcquire(key, limit): Future[Boolean]` wrapping the statement above, following the existing Anorm DAO + repository conventions (blocking DB pool, etc.). `true` = acquired, `false` = rejected.

The limiter key must be a Scala 3 `enum` (e.g. `RateLimitKey` with case `Bedrock`), mapped to its TEXT column value at the boundary — NOT a loose string (the repo prefers enums over stringly-typed values). Adding a limiter should be a new enum case.

The limit lives in CONFIG, not the table: add `bedrock.requestsPerMinute` (env `BEDROCK_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`) to the Bedrock config, with the window fixed at one minute. Do not add a config table or variable window sizes.

### 4. Wire into the Bedrock client (reject, don't wait)
In RealBedrockClient, before each `converse`/`suggest` call, call `tryAcquire(RateLimitKey.Bedrock, requestsPerMinute)`. Because both extraction and suggestions go through this one client, they share one budget. On `false`, return a failed Future with a typed `BedrockRateLimitedException` and do NOT call Bedrock. MockBedrockClient must always acquire (never rate-limit in tests).

### 5. Treat a throttle as transient, not terminal
In ExtractBankStatementDraftAction's `recoverWith`, distinguish:
- TRANSIENT: our `BedrockRateLimitedException`, or an AWS `ThrottlingException` / HTTP 429. On transient, do NOT markFailed. Let the exception propagate so the background-job runner (BackgroundJobTypeRunner) records the job failed with its existing backoff (`setStatusToFailed` with an `executeAt` derived from `errorCount`) and retries it later. The draft must stay in `processing` so the retried extraction job re-runs it (the action already skips drafts whose status is not `processing`).
- TERMINAL: everything else (unreadable PDF, classified as not-a-bank-statement, no transactions, etc.). Keep today's behaviour: markFailed with the message.

Never surface the raw AWS SDK exception string to the user.

ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction already retries with backoff; a rate-limit rejection there should flow into that existing retry path — do not add new retry machinery.

## Conventions (must follow)
- Follow docs/guide/ (architecture.md, backend.md, data-infra.md, testing.md, antipatterns.md, ci-checklist.md).
- No external API calls in tests; use the existing testcontainers Postgres for the DAO and fakes for the Bedrock client. Do not hit AWS.
- All list queries have ORDER BY; use Chimney for case-class shape mapping where it applies.
- Public repository: no PII anywhere in code, tests, comments, or the PR text.
- The PR description must NOT contain any claude.ai session link.

## Tests to add/adjust
- RateLimiter DAO: acquire succeeds and increments under the limit; the (limit+1)th acquire in the same minute is rejected; a call in a new minute resets the count to 1 and is granted; two keys are independent.
- RateLimitKey enum <-> TEXT mapping.
- RealBedrockClient (or a seam around it): when the limiter rejects, the call fails with BedrockRateLimitedException and Bedrock is never invoked (use a fake limiter/stub).
- ExtractBankStatementDraftAction: a transient rate-limit/throttle failure does NOT markFailed (draft stays `processing`, the job failure propagates so it is retried); a terminal failure still markFailed with the message. Extend the existing ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec.

## Acceptance criteria
- Under a burst, Bedrock calls beyond the configured per-minute limit are rejected by the limiter (not sent to AWS), and the affected extraction jobs are retried later with backoff rather than marking their drafts failed.
- A genuinely bad document still fails the draft terminally with a clean message (no raw SDK string).
- The rate-limit table holds at most one row per key and needs no cleanup job.
- All reads/writes follow repo conventions; the full test suite passes.

resultJson.description:
Uploading several bank statements close together makes some drafts end up `failed` and shows a raw AWS ThrottlingException/429 string in the UI. Extraction runs as a background job. Each draft fans out into several Bedrock `converse` calls through StatementExtractionService's ladder. ExtractBankStatementDraftAction catches every exception and marks the draft failed, so the job "succeeds" and is never retried. This epic (issue #119) adds a stateless, DB-backed admission-control rate limiter. Each Bedrock call first tries to take a per-minute slot. If no slot is free it fails fast with a typed `BedrockRateLimitedException` and never calls AWS. Throttles (our rejection or AWS's own ThrottlingException/429) are treated as transient: the draft stays `processing`, the job failure propagates, and BackgroundJobTypeRunner's existing backoff retries it later. Real document problems still fail the draft terminally with a clean message, never a raw SDK string.

The limiter is a single `rate_limit_window` table with one self-resetting row per key (key, window_start, count). An agreed atomic `INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE … WHERE … RETURNING count` statement consumes a slot. There is no cleanup job, no in-process state and no blocking wait. Keys are a Scala 3 enum (`RateLimitKey.Bedrock`), and the limit comes from config (`bedrock.requestsPerMinute` / `BEDROCK_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE`) with a fixed one-minute window. Both Bedrock entry points (`extractBankStatement` and `suggest`) go through RealBedrockClient, so they share one budget. MockBedrockClient never rate-limits.

Two findings refine the issue. (1) The rest of the ladder in StatementExtractionService swallows every exception. If that is left alone, a throttle there would quietly mark the draft `ready` with a weaker result instead of retrying it. So throttles must be re-raised there; Bedrock responses are cached in textract_cache, so a retry is cheap. (2) ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction and DocumentClassifier use JEV, not Bedrock, so they need no change; the suggestions action already re-raises for retry. The agreed SQL uses the database's `now()` on purpose, so all stateless instances share one clock. This differs from RULE-DB-016 (an injected Clock); keep the agreed SQL and explain why in a code comment.

tasks.title: Add rate_limit_window table, RateLimitKey enum, DAO and repository
tasks.description:
Add evolution `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/14.sql` (only a `-- !Ups` section) creating `rate_limit_window(key TEXT NOT NULL, window_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, count INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (key))`. No DEFAULT, no CHECK. Add a SQL comment that lists the allowed key values (`Bedrock`) and explains that there is one self-resetting row per key, so no cleanup is needed.

Add `net.wiringbits.models.RateLimitKey` as a Scala 3 `enum RateLimitKey extends DbEnum { case Bedrock }` with `object RateLimitKey extends DbEnum.Companion[RateLimitKey]`. The stored value is `entryName` (the case name).

Add `net.wiringbits.repositories.daos.RateLimitWindowDAO` with `def tryConsume(key: String, limit: Int)(implicit conn: Connection): Option[Int]`. It runs the agreed single statement exactly as given in the issue: INSERT … VALUES ({key}, date_trunc('minute', now()), 1) ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET window_start = date_trunc('minute', now()), count = CASE WHEN rate_limit_window.window_start = date_trunc('minute', now()) THEN rate_limit_window.count + 1 ELSE 1 END WHERE rate_limit_window.window_start < date_trunc('minute', now()) OR rate_limit_window.count < {limit} RETURNING count. Parse it with `SqlParser.int("count").singleOpt`. Never use SELECT-then-write. Add a short comment explaining that `now()` is used deliberately because the shared DB clock is the one clock for stateless instances.

Add `net.wiringbits.repositories.RateLimitWindowRepository @Inject()(database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext)` with `def tryAcquire(key: RateLimitKey, limit: Int): Future[Boolean] = Future { database.withConnection { implicit conn => RateLimitWindowDAO.tryConsume(key.entryName, limit).isDefined } }`. Register it in test `RepositoryComponents` and `RepositorySpec.withRepositories`.

Tests in a new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/repositories/RateLimitWindowRepositorySpec.scala`. The DB is shared, so DAO-level cases call `RateLimitWindowDAO.tryConsume` through `repositories.database.withConnection` with random `UUID.randomUUID().toString` keys:
- consecutive consumes under the limit return Some(1), Some(2), …
- the (limit+1)th consume in the same minute returns None and leaves the count unchanged
- a stale row (window_start moved back by at least one minute) resets to Some(1). Add a small helper in `utils/RepositoryUtils` to move the window back, because time is DB-side and can't be injected.
- two keys are independent
- repository-level: `tryAcquire(RateLimitKey.Bedrock, Int.MaxValue)` returns true

Also add a small `RateLimitKeySpec` checking that `Bedrock.entryName == "Bedrock"` and that `withNameOption` round-trips. Keep limits small, and put the burst tests in a single `withConnection` block so a minute rollover is unlikely.

Verify with `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *RateLimitWindowRepositorySpec *RateLimitKeySpec"`.

tasks.title: Gate RealBedrockClient behind the DB rate limiter (reject, don't wait)
tasks.description:
Config: add `requestsPerMinute: Int` to `BedrockConfig`, read from `config.get[Int]("requestsPerMinute")`, and include it in `toString`. In application.conf `bedrock {}` add `requestsPerMinute = <conservative default, e.g. 10>` and `requestsPerMinute = ${?BEDROCK_REQUESTS_PER_MINUTE}`, with a comment saying the window is fixed at one minute and the value should stay at or below the account's Bedrock quota. Add a row to the README env table. Update every `BedrockConfig(...)` call site: `scripts/AiExtractionProof.scala`, `scripts/StatementPipelineEval.scala` and `test/.../services/StatementExtractionServiceSpec.scala`.

Seam: `apis` may only reference `clientmodels` and `shared` (see server/.wartremover-layering.conf), so the client cannot touch a repository or a service.
- Add a `trait RateLimiter { def tryAcquire(key: RateLimitKey, limit: Int): Future[Boolean] }` in the shared layer (`net.wiringbits.util.RateLimiter`).
- Implement it in `net.wiringbits.services.DbRateLimiter @Inject()(repo: RateLimitWindowRepository) extends RateLimiter`, delegating to the repository.
- Bind it in `ServicesModule.configure()` with `bind(classOf[RateLimiter]).to(classOf[DbRateLimiter])`. Modules may reference services but not repositories.

Client:
- Add `class BedrockRateLimitedException(message: String) extends RuntimeException(message)` in `apis/BedrockClient.scala`, mirroring `JevRateLimitedException`.
- Change RealBedrockClient to `class RealBedrockClient(config: BedrockConfig, rateLimiter: RateLimiter, client: BedrockRuntimeAsyncClient)(implicit ec)`. Move the AWS client builder into the companion (e.g. `RealBedrockClient.awsClient(config)`), so tests can pass a fake.
- Add a private `guarded(call: => Future[ConverseResponse])` that runs `rateLimiter.tryAcquire(RateLimitKey.Bedrock, config.requestsPerMinute)`. On false it returns `Future.failed(new BedrockRateLimitedException(...))` without invoking `client.converse`. Use it in both `extractBankStatement` and `suggest`.
- Update the `ServicesModule.bedrockClient` provider to inject `RateLimiter` and build the real client. MockBedrockClient stays limiter-free.
- In the two scripts, pass an inline always-true `RateLimiter` with a comment (one-off ops tooling, single process) plus `RealBedrockClient.awsClient(config)`.

Tests: new `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/RealBedrockClientSpec.scala` with a hand-written fake `BedrockRuntimeAsyncClient` (implement `serviceName`/`close`, override `converse(ConverseRequest)` to count calls and return a `CompletableFuture.completedFuture` of a `ConverseResponse` built with one text block and stopReason END_TURN) and a stub `RateLimiter`. Cases:
- limiter false: `extractBankStatement` and `suggest` fail with `BedrockRateLimitedException` and the fake records 0 calls
- limiter true: the call goes through and returns the text
- the limiter receives `RateLimitKey.Bedrock` and the configured `requestsPerMinute`

No AWS calls. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "server/testOnly *RealBedrockClientSpec *StatementExtractionServiceSpec"`.

tasks.title: Treat Bedrock throttling as transient in draft extraction; keep terminal failures clean
tasks.description:
Add a classifier in the `BedrockClient` companion (apis/BedrockClient.scala), e.g. `def isThrottled(ex: Throwable): Boolean`. It walks the cause chain, because AWS async failures may arrive wrapped in `java.util.concurrent.CompletionException`, and returns true for `BedrockRateLimitedException`, `software.amazon.awssdk.services.bedrockruntime.model.ThrottlingException`, or any `software.amazon.awssdk.awscore.exception.AwsServiceException` with `statusCode() == 429`. Add a companion helper that detects an AWS SDK exception (`software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException`) anywhere in the chain, used for message sanitising.

ExtractBankStatementDraftAction.apply: change `run.recoverWith` so a throttled exception is not recovered. Log it at info/warn ("retrying via job backoff") and re-raise it so BackgroundJobTypeRunner records the failure and reschedules with `DelayGenerator` backoff. The draft stays `Processing`, so the retried job re-runs it. Every other exception keeps today's `markFailed`. If the exception chain contains an AWS SDK exception, store a fixed user-facing message (e.g. "The AI extraction service failed; please try uploading again.") instead of `ex.getMessage`, and log the raw exception. Keep the `reject` path unchanged. Update the class scaladoc, which currently says hard failures never propagate.

StatementExtractionService.extract: the `rung` helper's `.recover { case ex => … prev }` swallows everything. Narrow it to `case ex if !BedrockClient.isThrottled(ex)` so a throttle inside a later rung propagates and the draft retries, instead of quietly finishing `ready` with a weaker result. Cached Bedrock/BDA/Textract results in textract_cache make the retry cheap. The first rung already propagates.

Do not touch ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction. It uses JEV, not Bedrock, and already re-raises for retry.

Tests:
- Extend `ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec`. Use `stubJev("bank_statement", BigDecimal("0.97"))` and a Mockito `StatementExtractionService` whose `extract` returns `Future.failed(...)`.
  - (a) `BedrockRateLimitedException`: `apply(...).failed.futureValue` is that exception, the draft is still `Processing` and its `error` is None.
  - (b) AWS `ThrottlingException.builder().message(...).statusCode(429).build()` wrapped in a `CompletionException`: same assertions.
  - (c) terminal `RuntimeException("no usable result")`: the future succeeds, the draft is `Failed` and `error == Some("no usable result")`.
  - (d) a non-throttle AWS exception (e.g. `BedrockRuntimeException.builder().message("raw sdk text").statusCode(400).build()`): the draft is `Failed` with the clean message, and the error does not contain the raw SDK text.
- Add a `StatementExtractionServiceSpec` case where the first rung returns a non-reconciling result and the next Bedrock call fails with `BedrockRateLimitedException`. Assert that `extract` fails with it rather than returning the earlier result.
- Optionally add unit cases for `isThrottled`.

Verify with `CI=true sbt "server/testOnly *ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec *StatementExtractionServiceSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
Scala 3 / Play / Anorm / Guice backend in `server/`. Read docs/guide/{architecture,backend,data-infra,testing,antipatterns}.md. Package layering is enforced at compile time by `server/.wartremover-layering.conf`. Key edges: `apis` → only {clientmodels, shared}; `services` → {services, repositories, apis, dbmodels, shared}; `repositories` → {daos, dbmodels, shared}; `modules` → {apis, services, shared, tasks} (NOT repositories); `scripts` → {apis, daos, repositories, services, dbmodels, shared}; `actions` → {services, validations, repositories, apis, dbmodels, shared}. Shared = net.wiringbits.{models, config, executors, util, api, common}. So RealBedrockClient (apis) can only depend on the limiter through a trait in `net.wiringbits.util`, implemented in `services` and bound in `modules`.

Key files:
- `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/apis/BedrockClient.scala`: trait with `extractBankStatement(statementText: String, feedback: Option[String] = None): Future[String]` and `suggest(prompt: String): Future[String]`. A new exception and classifier go here (precedent: `class JevRateLimitedException(message: String) extends RuntimeException(message)` in apis/JevClient.scala).
- `apis/RealBedrockClient.scala`: today `class RealBedrockClient(config: BedrockConfig)(implicit ec)` builds `BedrockRuntimeAsyncClient` inline (Netty, 120s read timeout) and calls `client.converse(request).asScala` (scala.jdk.FutureConverters) in both methods.
- `apis/MockBedrockClient.scala`: returns canned JSON; must stay limiter-free.
- `config/BedrockConfig.scala`: case class plus `apply(Configuration)` that reads keys under `bedrock {}`, with a custom `toString`.
- `server/src/main/resources/application.conf`: `bedrock {}` block (around line 175); each key is a default followed by `${?ENV}`.
- `modules/ServicesModule.scala`: `@Provides @Singleton def bedrockClient(config: BedrockConfig, ec: ExecutionContext): BedrockClient` matches on Mock/Real; `configure()` holds the `bind(...)` calls.
- Other `new RealBedrockClient(config)` / `BedrockConfig(...)` call sites: `scripts/AiExtractionProof.scala`, `scripts/StatementPipelineEval.scala`, `test/.../services/StatementExtractionServiceSpec.scala` (named args).
- `actions/bankstatements/ExtractBankStatementDraftAction.scala`: `apply(draftId)` skips non-Processing drafts. `run.recoverWith { case ex => markFailed(draftId, ex.getMessage, clock.instant()) }` is the line to split into transient vs terminal. Repository: `bankStatementDraftRepository.markFailed(id, msg, Instant)`. Status enum: `repositories.models.BankStatementDraft.Status.{Processing, Ready, Failed}`.
- `services/StatementExtractionService.scala`: in `extract`, the first rung is uncovered and the later rungs go through a `rung(...)` helper whose `.recover { case ex => prev }` swallows everything. `cachedExtractBankStatement` caches Bedrock raw output in textract_cache (apiType "bedrock_extraction"), so retries are cheap.
- `tasks/BackgroundJobTypeRunner.scala`: on a failed future it calls `setStatusToFailed(job.id, executeAt = now + DelayGenerator.createDelay(errorCount) minutes (2^n), ex.getMessage)`. This is the retry path; add no new retry machinery. Extract job settings: parallelism 2, timeout 6 min (config/BackgroundJobsExecutorConfig.scala).
- `actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala` and `services/DocumentClassifier` use JEV, not Bedrock, so no change is needed. The suggestions action already re-raises for retry.

DB conventions:
- Evolutions live in `server/src/main/resources/evolutions/default/`; the highest is 13.sql, so the new one is 14.sql. Only `-- !Ups`, never `-- !Downs`. No DEFAULT, no CHECK, no SQL ENUM. Enum columns are TEXT with a comment listing values. One evolution file per PR.
- DAOs are `object XDAO` with `import anorm.*` and `SQL"""..."""` interpolation and are synchronous with `(implicit conn: Connection)`. No logging, no Future. Example: `repositories/daos/TextractCacheDAO.scala`; shared parsers/columns live in `repositories/daos/package.scala`.
- Repositories are `class XRepository @Inject()(database: Database)(implicit ec: DatabaseExecutionContext)` and wrap the whole body in `Future { database.withConnection/withTransaction { implicit conn => DAO... } }`. Example: `repositories/TextractCacheRepository.scala`.
- DB enums follow `net.wiringbits.models.DbEnum`: `enum X extends DbEnum { case A }` plus `object X extends DbEnum.Companion[X]` (`entryName` = case name; `withNameOption`, `withNameInsensitiveOption`). Example: `models/documents/DocumentKind.scala`.
- The agreed rate-limit SQL uses `date_trunc('minute', now())` on purpose (shared DB clock across stateless instances). Keep it verbatim. It differs from RULE-DB-016 (injected Clock), so justify it in a comment. No SELECT-then-write.

Testing:
- ScalaTest AnyWordSpec with `Matchers` (must). `should`/`in` names describe behaviour, never the class name. Test files mirror source paths.
- DB specs extend `net.wiringbits.core.RepositorySpec`, which gives `withRepositories() { implicit repositories => ... }` and `repositories.database`. Factories come from `utils.RepositoryUtils` (e.g. `createUser()`, `createBankStatementDraft(userId, storageKey = ...)`).
- The Postgres testcontainer is SHARED across the test JVM, so use random unique keys/values. Repositories are constructed in `core/RepositorySpec.withRepositories` and listed in `core/RepositoryComponents`; add new ones to both.
- Use `.futureValue` for results and `.failed.futureValue` for expected failures. Mockito (`MockitoSugar`) is already used in ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec. Hand-written fakes are preferred where easy.
- ExtractBankStatementDraftActionSpec already has `InMemoryBlobStorage`, `stubJev(choice, confidence)`, a synthetic `statementPdf`, `extractionService()` (a Mockito mock of `StatementExtractionService.extract(anyString x4)`), and `action(jevClient, service)`. Reuse them.
- `BedrockRuntimeAsyncClient` is an interface whose methods have defaults; only `serviceName()` and `close()` are abstract, so a hand-written fake is easy. Build responses with `ConverseResponse.builder().output(ConverseOutput.builder().message(Message.builder().role(ConversationRole.ASSISTANT).content(ContentBlock.fromText("...")).build()).build()).stopReason(StopReason.END_TURN).build()`.
- AWS exception builders: `ThrottlingException.builder().message(..).statusCode(429).build()`, `BedrockRuntimeException.builder()...` (package software.amazon.awssdk.services.bedrockruntime.model). Base classes: `software.amazon.awssdk.awscore.exception.AwsServiceException`, `software.amazon.awssdk.core.exception.SdkException`.
- Never call AWS in tests.

Build and verify: `CI=true` turns on -Werror and the warts (Any, ToString and Layering are enforced). Run targeted tests only: `CI=true sbt \"server/testOnly *SpecName\"` or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Do not run the full `sbt test`. Format with `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt`. Web tests need Node 24, which doesn't matter here because the work is server-only.

Other rules:
- No default parameter values in new code (a reviewer rule).
- Prefer enums over strings.
- Fail loudly; never invent data.
- No PII in code, tests or comments; use synthetic data only.
- The PR text must not include any claude.ai session link.

findings.title: RateLimiter trait and its DbRateLimiter implementation are split across two files

reason.text: The layering rules (server/.wartremover-layering.conf) don't allow it. `apis` may only call {clientmodels, shared}, so the trait has to stay in shared (`util`) for RealBedrockClient to use it. `shared` may only call `shared`, so DbRateLimiter, which depends on RateLimitWindowRepository, can't live there. Moving the trait into `services` would break RealBedrockClient. Letting `util` reach `repositories` would weaken the layering the task says must hold. The split is the seam the plan agreed on. The non-DB implementation (AlwaysGrant) now sits in the trait's companion.
